cards.title: Summer holidays: Learn from orangutans about playdates
cards.body: Scientists say that messing about and play have health benefits for humans of all ages. With six weeks of childcare to arrange, parents can take inspiration from how orangutans arrange playdates for their offspring.

cards.title: New mothers deserve policy support, not just incentives
cards.body: Research reveals deep anxieties among new mothers about falling birthrates and societal pressure. Rather than medals and cash bonuses, policy should address women's real concerns about motherhood.

cards.title: The hidden mistake parents make when praising children
cards.body: The words you choose when praising your child matter more than you think. Science-backed praise can help children build confidence, resilience, and a lifelong love of learning.

cards.title: Connect with adopted and foster children effectively
cards.body: All adopted and foster children come with one or multiple childhood adversities that require understanding. Learn principles and strategies for successfully parenting at-risk children.

cards.title: Break the cycle: Don't pass childhood trauma to kids
cards.body: Many parents carry trauma or dysfunction from their own childhoods. By understanding your own triggers, you can break the cycle and prevent passing trauma to your children.

cards.title: Stop bailing out your adult child with 'loans'
cards.body: That loan you'll never collect to your adult child isn't generosity—it's a bribe to feel like a good parent. Understand the difference between healthy support and enabling behavior.
